claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 6.8 earthquake on 28 July 2026 at 07:27:15 UTC, 5 km E of Uto, Japan (32.6817N, 130.7217E), at a depth of approximately 10 km.

Re-checked 7 August 2026: USGS's PAGER loss-model product for event us6000tgb9 is unchanged since its 29 July 2026 update (alert level Red, empirical estimate 724 fatalities / semi-empirical 234 fatalities, ~$12.7 billion economic loss) -- these remain automated model estimates, not confirmed figures. No allowlisted source (USGS, GDACS, ReliefWeb, WHO) has published a confirmed casualty or damage figure as of 7 August 2026.
USGS's PAGER system assessed an overall Red alert level for this earthquake (economic-loss alert Red, fatality alert Yellow), with a maximum estimated shaking intensity of MMI VIII (Severe).

USGS's PAGER population-exposure estimate for this earthquake found about 1,422,182 people exposed to MMI VII (Very Strong) shaking or greater and about 8,057,091 additional people exposed to MMI V (Moderate) shaking, almost entirely within Japan (a small population of about 65 people in South Korea was exposed to MMI III, weak, shaking).

USGS PAGER's loss-model data, updated 29 July 2026, records a maximum shaking intensity of MMI IX, a fatality alert level of Orange (gvalue 1.77, up from Yellow) and an economic alert level of Red (gvalue 2.28). Aggregated population exposure at MMI VII or greater is about 1,236,912 (374,783 at MMI VII + 635,782 at MMI VIII + 226,347 at MMI IX). PAGER's empirical loss model estimates 724 total fatalities (0 in South Korea) and $12,724,898,845 in economic losses; PAGER's semi-empirical structural model separately estimates 234 fatalities. These are automated probabilistic model outputs, not confirmed casualty or damage figures.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: USGS's event page (id us6000tgb9) shows no PAGER product update since 29 July 2026 and no dedicated OCHA/ReliefWeb situation report exists for this earthquake; the Red/Orange PAGER alert levels and probabilistic loss estimates are unchanged, and no confirmed casualty or damage figures have been published.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: USGS's PAGER loss-model product (version 7, processed 29 July 2026) remains the latest; no confirmed casualty or damage figures have been published by an allowlisted source as of 2 August 2026.

Re-checked 3 August 2026: USGS's feed for event us6000tgb9 (last updated 29 July 2026) still shows the Red/Orange PAGER alert and the same loss-model estimates as the prior check; no GDACS report and no allowlisted confirmed casualty or damage figure exists for this earthquake as of 3 August 2026.

Re-checked 5 August 2026: USGS's feed for event us6000tgb9 shows an 'updated' timestamp of 1785818703869 (29 July 2026), with the alert level still 'red' and maximum MMI 9.243; no PAGER product update, no GDACS report, and no allowlisted confirmed casualty or damage figure exists for this earthquake as of 5 August 2026.

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: USGS's feed for event us6000tgb9 remains unchanged since the 29 July 2026 PAGER update (Alert Level Red, Max MMI 9.0/Violent, update time 2026-07-28T20:01:53Z); no allowlisted source has published a confirmed casualty or damage figure as of 6 August 2026.

description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck southern Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu, Japan, on 28 July 2026 at 07:27 UTC (16:27 local time), 5 km east of Uto City, at a depth of about 10 km. USGS's PAGER system initially assessed an overall Red alert level (economic-loss alert Red, fatality alert Yellow) with a maximum estimated shaking intensity of MMI VIII (Severe); a PAGER loss-model update as of 29 July 2026 raised the maximum estimated shaking to MMI IX (Violent) and upgraded the fatality alert from Yellow to Orange, with the economic alert remaining Red — PAGER's probabilistic loss models now estimate roughly 724 fatalities (empirical model) or 234 fatalities (semi-empirical structural model) and about $12.7 billion in economic losses. About 1.24 million people were exposed to MMI VII (Very Strong) shaking or greater, almost entirely within Japan. As of 3 August 2026, these remain PAGER's automated probabilistic estimates — no allowlisted authoritative source has yet published confirmed casualty or damage figures, though non-allowlisted international media report a Japanese-government-confirmed death toll that had risen into the mid-30s by 1 August. Re-checked 5 August 2026: USGS's event page and feed for us6000tgb9 still show no PAGER product update since 29 July 2026; no allowlisted source has published confirmed casualty or damage figures.

PAGER's probabilistic loss models now estimate about 724 fatalities (empirical) or 234 fatalities (semi-empirical) and about $12.7 billion in economic losses — these are automated model estimates, not confirmed figures. No allowlisted source has yet published confirmed casualty or damage figures.
